ca_8_dostie.blurb: Dostie is a young, still-developing wall in the June Lake backcountry of the Eastern Sierra, one sector of the Rush crag at roughly 7,300 feet. It holds about two dozen routes split among sport, top-rope and trad, mostly easy to mid-grade lines with a few around 5.10 and one 5.11 at the top end. The wall faces west-southwest, with a slanting slab at lower left, a steeper wall at lower right and upright fins above. The rock has seen little traffic and can be loose, so a helmet, care under other parties and backup for anchors are sensible. Expect a quiet, pioneering feel rather than a polished sport crag.
ca_8_dostie.approach: From the neighbouring sector below, turn off and climb a steep, brushy slope of dirt, grass and sagebrush, about 200 vertical feet. Allow roughly 10 to 20 minutes.

ca_banana_belt.blurb: Banana Belt is a sector of the Central Gorge in Owens River Gorge, a deep volcanic-tuff canyon outside Bishop in the Eastern Sierra. Nearly all of its roughly two dozen routes are bolted sport lines, with a few trad options mixed in. The grades start around 5.7, but most climbs sit in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a couple pushing 5.12, so it suits intermediate to strong climbers. Routes are single pitch and fairly long, around 100 to 150 feet. The gorge is a dense, well-bolted sport destination that is easy to reach from town, and the Central Gorge walls around this sector tend to be busy.

ca_west_face_left_side.blurb: This is the left-hand section of the West Face of Tahquitz Rock, the larger of the two granite domes above Idyllwild in the San Jacinto Mountains, at about 7,400 feet. Climbing here is almost entirely traditional, in multi-pitch lines of three to four pitches. A few easy routes sit at the bottom of the range, but the bulk of the two dozen climbs fall between 5.8 and 5.11, and the largest group is around 5.10. It is a classic Southern California trad setting, so bring a full rack and expect to share the cliff with other parties on good weekends.

ca_siberia.blurb: Siberia is the biggest formation in the Outer Mongolia group in the Wonderland area of Joshua Tree National Park. Its large south-leaning face carries mostly one- and two-pitch bolted lines, while shorter trad climbs line the shaded corridor on the other side. About two dozen routes run from roughly 5.6 to 5.11, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.10, so there is plenty for moderate climbers. The hike in is long enough that crowds are thin, and the place feels remote and wild. The rock is brown granite with the usual Joshua Tree texture.
ca_siberia.approach: Follow the well-worn trail north from the lot, taking the right branch toward Willow Hole. After about two miles a marker shows where to leave the trail; an unclear path and some boulder hopping lead to the base. Count on about an hour in total.

ca_drug_dome.blurb: Drug Dome is a small granite dome in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite National Park, just west of Fairview Dome at about 9,000 feet. Close to the road yet less visited than its neighbours, it is unusually steep for Tuolumne, and its north side holds the headline lines. Most of the roughly two dozen routes are traditional, with a couple of sport lines. Grades span the 5.7s up to 5.14, but the weight is in the 5.10s and 5.11s, so it rewards strong leaders comfortable on face climbing and cracks. Some routes are multi-pitch. A small ice line is also listed.

ca_san_ysidro.blurb: San Ysidro is a sandstone canyon crag above Montecito in Santa Barbara, ringed by thick vegetation. Climbs here are mostly traditional, with a handful of sport routes and one top-rope line. The wall offers everything from technical slabs to steeper, sporty climbing, and the grades run from about 5.6 to 5.12, with plenty of routes between 5.7 and 5.11. Several lines are thinly protected, so confident leading helps. The dense foliage holds moisture, so it dries slowly after rain. It is considered some of the best canyon climbing in the area and draws a few parties on weekends.
ca_san_ysidro.parking_note: From Highway 101 take the San Ysidro exit, then follow East Valley Road, Park Lane and Mountain Drive uphill and leave the car along there.
ca_san_ysidro.approach: From the car, walk through the residential backyards to a fire road and follow it about five minutes. Turn left just before the gate and cross the stream to reach the base.

ca_hayfork_haven_the.blurb: The Hayfork Haven is a recently developed wall in far northwest California, in the Redwood Coast climbing region, a long drive inland from the coast. Over twenty lines cover a wide spread: mostly traditional, plus some sport routes and a few easy boulder problems. Grades go from beginner-friendly slabs in the 5.4 range up to 5.12, and the largest cluster is 5.10 and 5.11. The stone is fluted and juggy, and protection is often sparse, with bolts only where gear will not go, so the crag suits climbers who are comfortable placing their own gear. The setting is quiet and forested, with a quick walk from the road.

ca_western_royal_arches.blurb: Western Royal Arches is the left-hand end of the Royal Arches cliff on the north side of Yosemite Valley, below North Dome and beside Washington Column, at around 4,300 feet. The granite here is climbed mainly with traditional gear, in single- and multi-pitch lines, with a small number of bolted and top-rope options. Grades start near 5.7 and most climbs fall in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a couple at 5.12, so it is better for climbers with some experience than for newcomers. Arch-shaped exfoliation features shape the wall. Routes catch afternoon sun, and a short climbers' trail from the Valley Loop Trail leads in.
